text:
Priya: quick question — we're seeing a few customer routes where request logging samples full prompt text even though their consent flag is off. who owns making consent propagate to the request/response logger?
Alex: Platform owns the logger surface, but product owns the consent semantics. We need a small contract: route metadata -> logger policy.
Sam: Agree. Practically we should have 3 route-level flags: consent: explicit_opt_in / opt_out / unknown. Logger then treats explicit_opt_in as full capture, opt_out as redact, unknown follows tenant default.
Maria: +1. Also need an 'inspector_breakglass' boolean for support but auditable with TTL.
Priya: here's a config stub I sketched — open to bikeshedding:
```yaml
routes:
  /generate-summaries:
    logging:
      consent: opt_out    # opt_in | opt_out | unknown
      redact_policy: pii_hmac
      inspector_breakglass: ttl: 3600
```
Alex: two implementation questions: (1) where does the redact transform run (edge proxy vs logging pipeline), (2) how does sampling interact with redaction? if we sample before redaction we leak.
Sam: must redact before sampling. pipeline order: receive -> apply route policy -> redact -> sample -> persist/forward. doing it the other way is unacceptable.
Maria: for performance we can do lightweight deterministic hashing at the gateway (fast HMAC) and full redaction enrichment downstream for queued records. gateway HMAC is enough for immediate indexing/metrics.
Devex Bot: FYI — tagging: @devex is tracking console UX for per-route consent toggles.
Alex: console UX: show effective logging policy (route-level override + tenant default + org policy). Also show a clear audit trail: who toggled breakglass, TTL, and reason.
Priya: about quotas — if we redact heavily we reduce signal for usage-based chargebacks. product asked for granular cost attribution. Any ideas?
Sam: add token-level counters that are independent of string content (counts only), and attach hashed request id for tie-backs when consent exists. That way chargeback works without storing PII.
Maria: we should also document allowed fields that can bypass redact for auditing (e.g., request_id, user_id_hash) and ensure those are minimal.
Priya: testing plan: canary in staging with two tenants — one with opt_in, one opt_out — verify no plaintext in logs for opt_out and that sampling rates match. Also run a quick privacy audit script to search for email/@ tokens.
Alex: ops concerns: if redact happens downstream and someone queries tracing, they might expect full payload. Need to expose a 'request_viewer' feature gated by breakglass + audit.
Maria: agreed. breakglass must emit an immutable audit record including who, why, and a signed short-lived token. No unlogged access.
Devex Bot: checklist added to project board: /boards/infra/privacy-propagation (https://redwood.internal/boards/infra/privacy-propagation) :eyes:
Priya: timeline proposal: RFC this week, implement gateway HMAC + console display next sprint, downstream redaction and audit mid next quarter. Any objections?
Sam: no objections. I'll draft the RFC with ordering guarantees and perf numbers for gateway HMAC.
Maria: I'll prototype the audit event schema and TTL enforcement.
Alex: I'll own console effective-policy UI and breakglass audit integration.
Priya: thanks folks. if anyone spots a route that still logs plaintext after the change ping me and dump sample ts+route. :thumbsup:
Ops Bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout of gateway HMAC added to staging (canary-3) — 1768890200.
Maria: ran privacy grep on staging logs after canary — no obvious email or credit-card patterns in captured logs for opt_out tenant. dropping sample artifacts to /artifacts/privacy/grep-1768890250.zip
Priya: perfect, closing loop. we'll collect metrics and reconvene post-RFC.
